questions.question: What is the average of the first six prime numbers?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

First six prime numbers i.e. 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13

**Formula used:**

Average = Sum elements/Number of elements

**Calculation:**

Average = (2 + 3 + 5 + 7 + 11 + 13)/6

⇒ 41/6

⇒ 6{5over6}

**∴ Required average is 6{5over6}**.

questions.question: A reduction of 20% in the price of bananas enables a customer to buy 6 more bananas for ₹80. What is the reduced price of bananas per dozen (in ₹)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A reduction of 20% in the price of bananas enables a customer to buy 6 more bananas for ₹80

**Calculation:**

Let the C.P of each banana be x

Total number of bananas in ₹ 80 = 80/x

New price = x – x × (20/100)

⇒ (100 - 20)x/100

⇒ 80x/100 or 4x/5

New number of bananas in ₹80 = 80/(4x/5)

⇒ 80/(4x/5)

⇒ 100/x

⇒ (100/x) – (80/x) = 6 

⇒ 20/x = 6 

⇒ x = 20/6

New price of bananas = 20/6 × 4/5

⇒ 8/3

The reduced price of bananas per dozen = (8/3) × 12

⇒ 32

**∴ The reduced price of bananas per dozen (in ₹) is 32.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ **

Let the original price of a banana be 5x, new price will be 4x(reduced by 20%)

Now, according to the question,

⇒ 80over 4x - 80over 5x = 6

⇒ {80 (5 - 4)}over 4 times 5 times x = 6

⇒ {80 (5 - 4)}over 20 times x = 6

⇒ 4over x = 6

⇒ x = 2over3

The new price of bananas is,

⇒ 4x = 4 ×2over3

The price per dozen is

⇒ 4 × 2over3 × 12 = 32

questions.question: The simple interest on a sum of money at 10% per annum for 4 years is ₹3,200. What will be the amount (in ₹) of the same sum for the same period at the same rate of interest when the interest is compounded annually?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The simple interest on a sum of money at 10% per annum for 4 years is ₹3200.

**Concept used:**

S.I = (P × T × R)/100

C.I = P(1 + R/100)T

Here,

P = Sum

R = Rate

T = Time

**Calculation:**

Let the sum be P

According to the question,

3200 = (P × 4 × 10)/100

⇒ P = 3200 × (10/4)

⇒ P = 8000

So, sum is Rs. 8000

Now,

A = 8000(1 + 10/100)⁴

⇒ A = 8000(1 + 1/10)4

⇒ A = 8000(11/10)4

⇒ A = 8000(14641/10000)

⇒ A = 11712.80

**∴ The amount (in ₹) of the same sum for the same period at the same rate of interest when the interest is compounded annually is 11712.80**

questions.question: In ΔPQR, ∠Q = 66° and ∠R = 34°. T is a point on QR , and S is a point between Q and T such that PS ⊥ QR and PT is the bisector of ∠QPR. What is the measure of ∠SPT?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

PS ⊥ QR

∠Q = 66° and ∠R = 34°

PT is the bisector of ∠QPR

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/635fd8edbaa3e86aed5907cc464d684940975e0a792ef720a4a96bd88e6be94c.png] 

∠QPR = 180° - 66° - 34°

⇒ 80°

∠QPT = ∠TPR = 40° [As PT angle bisector]

In Δ PTR

∠PTR + ∠PRT + ∠TPR = 180° 

⇒ ∠PTR = 180° - 34° - 40°

⇒ ∠PTR = 106°

Now,

∠PTS + ∠PTR = 180°

⇒ ∠PTS + 106° = 180°

⇒ ∠PTS = 180° - 106°

⇒ ∠PTS = 74°

So,

∠SPT = 180° - 90° - 74°

⇒ ∠SPT = 16°

**∴ The measure of ∠SPT is 16°.**

questions.question: A, B and C divide an amount of ₹10,500 amount themselves in the ratio 5 : 7 : 9, respectively. If each one gets ₹500 more, then what will be the ratio of the amounts with A,B and C?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A, B and C divide an amount of ₹10,500 amount themselves in the ratio 5 : 7 : 9, respectively. 

**Calculation:**

Share of A = 10500 × 5/21

⇒ 2500

Share of B = 10500 × 7/21

⇒ 3500

Share of C = 10500 × 9/21

⇒ 4500

If each 500 more then the amount got by A, B and C = 3000, 4000, 5000

questions.question: A fruit vendor recovers the cost of 95 oranges by selling 80 oranges. What is his profit percentage?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A fruit vendor recovers the cost of 95 oranges by selling 80 oranges

**Calculation:**

According to the question,

CP of 95 oranges = SP of 80 oranges

⇒ CP/SP = 80/95

⇒ CP/SP = 16/19

So, ratio of CP : SP = 16 : 19

So profit = 19 - 16

⇒ 3

Profit % = (3/16) × 100

⇒ 18.75

**∴ His profit percentage is 18.75%.**

questions.question: A and B are two points on the same side of a ground, 50 meters apart. The angles of elevation of these points to the top of a tree are 60° and 30°, respectively. What is 40% of the height of the tree (in m)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A and B are two points on the same side of the ground, 50 meters apart.

The angles of elevation of these points to the top of a tree are 60° and 30°, respectively.

**Concept used:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a5b1d4c013ba48593ecefffec281fc4d35d5aabb012b4ee9d0e2ecec2607aad.png] 

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c7b320d2d4b3152fcfe4f55896cf32607fad8110c545b623e6396948d416cb57.png] 

Let the height of the tree be T and the distance between the foot of the tree to the point A be x

Now,

T/x = tan60°

⇒ T/x = √3

⇒ T = √3x

Again,

T/(x + 50) = tan30°

⇒ T/(x + 50) = 1/√3

⇒ T = (x + 50)/√3

Now,

√3x = (x + 50)/√3

⇒ 3x = x + 50

⇒ 2x = 50

⇒ x = 25

Now,

T/25 = √3

⇒ T = 25√3

So, height of the tree = 25√3 m

Now,

40% of the height of the tree = 25√3 × 40%

⇒ 10√3

**∴ 40% of the height of the tree (in m) is 10√3.**

Athletic club of 232 members and their height's frequency.

Y - co-ordinate = frequency of point = 0

questions.question: If the number 48k2048p6 is divisible by 99, then (k × p) is equal to:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

48k2048p6 is divisible by 99

**Concept used:**

If the sum of digits of the number is divisible by 9, then the number itself is divisible by 9.

If the difference of the sum of alternative digits of a number is divisible by 11 or 0, then that number is divisible by 11 completely.

**Calculation:**

99 = 9 × 11

So, the number should be divisible by both 9 and 11

Now,

4 + 8 + k + 2 + 0 + 4 + 8 + p + 6 = 32 + k + p

Now,

Possible values of k + p = 4, 13

Again,

(4 + k + 0 + 8 + 6) - (8 + 2 + 4 + p) = 0 or multiple of 11

⇒ 18 + k - 14 - p = 0 or multiple of 11

⇒ 4 + k - p = 0 or multiple of 11

Now, 

k - p can be - 4 or 7

Now,

For k + p = 4 and k - p = - 4

We can say by adding both 2k = 0

⇒ k = 0

So, p = 4 [Both are possible]

Again,

For k + p = 4 and k - p = 7

We can say by adding both 2k = 11

⇒ k = 5.5 [Not possible]

Again,

For k + p = 13 and k - p = - 4

We can say by adding both 2k = 9

⇒ k = 4.5 [Not possible]

Again,

For k + p = 13 and k - p = 7

We can say by adding both 2k = 20

⇒ k = 10 [Not possible]

So, only possible values of k and p is 0 and 4

Now,

k × p = 0 × 4

⇒ 0

**∴ Required answer is 0.**

questions.question: The least number which should be added to 3627 so that the sum is exactly divisible by 4, 5, 6 and 8 is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The number are 4, 5, 6 and 8

**Concept used:**

The least number which is exactly divisible by a, b and c is the L.C.M of a, b and c

**Calculation:**

LCM of 4, 5, 6 and 8 is 120

Now,

By dividing 120 from 3627 we get 27 as the remainder

So,

Required number which should be added to the next multiple of 120 = 120 - 27

⇒ 93

**∴ The required number is 93.**

questions.question: AC is the diameter of a circle dividing the circle into two semicircles. ED is a chord in one semicircle, such that ED is parallel to AC. B is a point on the circumference of the circle in the other semicircle. ∠CBE = 75°. What is the measure (in degrees) of ∠CED?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

∠CBE = 75°

**Concept used:**

The diameter of a circle subtends an angle of 90° at any point on the circle.

Angles formed by the endpoints of the chord in either major or minor segments are always equal.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f0227e0fefe168e2983b1128be44c552039338e77d896dba6bf7d918e170a97b.png] 

∠CBE = ∠CAE = 75° [Angles formed by the endpoints of the chord in either major or minor segments are always equal.]

∠AEC = 90° [The angle subtended from a diameter is 90]

So,

∠ECA = 180° - 90° - 75°

⇒ 15°

Now,

ED ∥ AC

So, ∠ECA = ∠CED = 15°

**∴ The measure (in degrees) of ∠CED is 15°.**

questions.question: AB is a chord in the minor segment of a circle with center O. C is a point between A and B on the minor arc AB. The tangents to the circle at A and B meet at the point D. If ∠ACB = 116°, then the measure of ∠ADB is

∠ACB = 116°

**Concept Used:**

When a quadrilateral is inscribed in a circle, the opposite angles of it are supplementary angles.

The angle subtended at the center is always double the angle subtended at the remaining arc.

The radius from the center of the circle to the point of tangency is perpendicular to the tangent line.

Point P is taken on the major arc of the circle.

Then, A & P, B & P, C & B, and A & C are joined.

From cyclic quadrilateral APBC

∠ACB = 116°

Now, ∠APB = (180 – 116)° = 64°

Now, ∠AOB = (64 × 2)°

⇒ 128°

Since OA = OB = radius of the circle

So, from quadrilateral AOBD

∠ADB = 360° - (∠OBD + ∠OAD + ∠AOB)

⇒ ∠ADB = 360° - (90° + 90° + 128°)

⇒ ∠ADB = 360° - 308°

⇒ ⇒ ∠ADB = 52° 

**∴ The required measure of ∠ADB is 52°.**
